title: Reading Arrears and Daily Ceilings across an Employee's Whole Portfolio
content:
Where an employee holds more than one Employee Meal Account, the two figures that decide what they may do are read across the whole portfolio rather than one account at a time.

**Arrears.** Arrears are summed across every account the employee holds under the same employer account code, and it is that total that is measured against the restriction threshold printed against the plan of the account being restricted.

**The daily spend ceiling.** The daily spend ceiling, by contrast, is read on each account separately, because each site's tills price and cap their own service day.

## Allowance does not travel

Employer allowance never moves between accounts: allowance granted on one site's account is spent at that site's eligible outlets and lapses there, whatever the employee holds elsewhere.

## Two employer account codes

Where the employee's accounts sit under two different employer account codes, the two portfolios are kept apart entirely and neither arrears nor allowance is read across them.

## What a restriction on one account does to the others

A restriction applied on one account does not restrict the others by itself; each account is restricted on its own record once the portfolio arrears total is what the threshold is measured against.

## The same rule put as a table

| Quantity | Read across the portfolio | Read on one account |
|---|---|---|
| Charges awaiting payroll recovery | Yes, summed under one employer account code | No |
| The daily spend ceiling | No | Yes, on each account's own service day |
| Unspent employer allowance | No, it never moves between accounts | Yes, at that site's eligible outlets |
| The restricted state itself | No | Yes, applied on each account's own record |
